problem: Collision-free DRL visual navigation agents are hard to train because enforcing collision avoidance makes rewards sparse, and uniform task sampling (the standard) fails to learn. Prior automatic curriculum methods such as GoalGAN are unstable and not tailored to navigation.
motivation: Collision-free policies and frozen real-image feature encoders are needed for Sim2Real transfer, but agents trained with simulator collision exploits (sliding along walls) do not transfer. A curriculum that picks tasks of appropriate difficulty from cheap geometric features can make sparse-reward training tractable and enable semantic-target navigation on real robots without retraining.
key_idea: NavACL trains a small classifier that predicts task success probability from geometric start/goal properties, and uses it to sample a mixture of easy, frontier (near-average difficulty, adaptive) and random tasks for PPO training.
insight: The adaptive boundary (mean and std of predicted success over random tasks) lets the curriculum track the policy as it improves. NavACL-Adaptive beat both NavACL-GOID and GoalGAN in the ablation on Cooperstown, while GOID performed on par with GoalGAN, so the adaptive component is what matters. Frozen mid-level features plus a COCO Mask R-CNN target mask allow swapping the target class at test time and transferring to real robots.
method: NavACL success predictor: a fully-connected net f_π maps geometric task features (geodesic distance, path complexity, turn angle sin/cos, agent/goal clearance, agent/goal island) to success probability; trained online with log loss on rollouts, no pretraining

Adaptive task mixture: sample random tasks and fit a normal (μf, σf) to f_π; easy tasks have f_π>μf+βσf, frontier tasks lie within μf±γσf (β=1, γ=0.1); random-task probability min(0.15, t/tmax), the rest split equally between easy and frontier
NavACL-GOID variant: selects tasks with 0.4≤f_π≤0.6 (goals of intermediate difficulty)
Reward shaping: r = 1succ + δ(−1coll + 1expl) + 0.01d, with collision penalty and episode termination, an exploration bonus for reaching new positions, δ=0.25
Frozen feature networks: spatial autoencoders pretrained on real images (depth, reshading, semantic) from Sax et al., frozen, compressed by conv layers
Semantic target network: COCO Mask R-CNN (FPN) mask for the target label, weighted by confidence and max-pooled, so the target class can be changed at runtime
Policy: PPO actor-critic with LSTM memory

setting.backbone: PPO actor-critic with conv compression + LSTM; frozen mid-level vision encoders (Sax et al.) and frozen COCO Mask R-CNN
setting.training_data: Habitat 2019 challenge Gibson training split, 20M timesteps, self-generated tasks from RL rollouts; encoders pretrained on real images/COCO
setting.observation: monocular RGB (converted to frozen latent features) plus semantic target label
setting.action_space: discrete motion primitives: turn ±30°, forward 0.2 m
setting.privileged: none at test time (simulator navmesh used only during training for curriculum geometry)

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 held-out scenes (Cooperstown, Avonia, Hometown), 10 trials of 30 episodes, football target, 150 step limit, max 10 m start-goal
numbers.evidence: Table III, NavACL Total: SR 0.42, SPL 0.24

numbers.eval_set_note: same 3 held-out scenes, target changed from football to a large vase at test time (unseen class)
numbers.extra: target swapped at test time, no retraining
numbers.evidence: Table III, NavACL Target-Agnostic Total: SR 0.36, SPL 0.17
Table III, PPO Baseline Total: SR 0.31, SPL 0.14

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, not a standard one. Ablation of curriculum methods on Cooperstown is only in figures. Real-world SPLs per trial are in Table IV (0.18–0.92) over 7 tasks. Human total SR 0.79 / SPL 0.56.
results: NavACL reaches total SR 0.42 / SPL 0.24 on unseen scenes vs PPO baseline 0.31 / 0.14, with random at 0.03 / 0.02. Humans achieve 0.79 / 0.56. Agents transfer without retraining to a Turtlebot3 (7 tasks, no collisions over 29 m) and partly to a Tello drone.
limitations: Performance drops sharply in larger unseen environments (Hometown SR 0.12), with weak LSTM memory and mirror-induced mirages
Very slow training (about 2 weeks for 20M steps) and a large gap to human performance
Small real-world evaluation (7 AGV tasks); UAV target detection unstable due to hover-height variation
builds_on: Sax et al. mid-level visual representations
